Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:

- FOMC stance remains clearly dovish and supportive (zero rates, ongoing QE in Treasuries and agency MBS, average inflation targeting, and explicit outcome-based forward guidance).
- SLOOS shows tighter lending standards and weaker demand in C&I/CRE and riskier consumer credit, while agency-eligible mortgages remain strong—implying policy support is most effective in housing but less so for business and subprime consumers.
- Beige Book adds that COVID-19 caused disruptions for producers and shippers, reinforcing supply chain constraints and operational challenges. These frictions, alongside renewed virus waves, weigh on near-term activity and hiring, and limit how quickly accommodative financial conditions can translate into real-economy gains.
- Net effect: Despite highly supportive policy, real-side bottlenecks (producers/shippers) and tighter bank credit temper the recovery impulse. Strong housing is a partial offset, but the Beige Book tilts the outlook more negative than the SLOOS-only view.
